howto.name: Upload an image
howto.text: Select a JPG, PNG, or WebP image up to 500 MB. Photos of people, products, and animals work best.

howto.name: Background removal runs automatically
howto.text: The server uses an AI model to detect the foreground subject and remove the background. No manual tracing is needed.

howto.name: Download the result
howto.text: Save the transparent PNG. You can also choose a solid-color replacement background before downloading.

faq.q: What kinds of photos work best?
faq.a: People, animals, products, and objects with clear edges work best. The U²-Net AI model handles fine details like hair, fur, and semi-transparent edges (sunglasses, leaves, water droplets) reasonably well — much better than the chroma-key technique on a green screen.

faq.q: Is the output a transparent PNG?
faq.a: Yes — the output is a 32-bit PNG with a real alpha channel. You can drop it onto any background in Figma, Canva, Photoshop, or PowerPoint and it composites cleanly. You can also pick a solid-color or image replacement background before downloading.

faq.q: Does it work on group photos with multiple people?
faq.a: Yes, but quality varies. The model is trained on single-subject portraits, so isolated people in a group are detected well. Overlapping bodies, faces in the background, and partial occlusions may need touch-up in an image editor.

faq.q: Is my photo uploaded somewhere external — like remove.bg?
faq.a: No. The U²-Net model runs on PrivaTools' own server inside an isolated Docker container. The photo enters temporary per-request storage, the model runs locally, the result is sent back, and both the input and output are unlinked from the temp directory immediately after the response. No third-party background-removal service is called.

500 MB per file, or 100 megapixels of pixel area — whichever you hit first. For most photography that's never a limit. RAW DSLR files at full resolution work; cropped product photos are well within bounds.

faq.q: How does this compare to remove.bg or Canva?
faq.a: Free with no daily quota or watermark (remove.bg adds a watermark on the free tier and caps at 1 image per session), no account required (Canva requires sign-up), and the entire pipeline is open source so you can self-host it. Quality is comparable to remove.bg's free tier.
